question: Guru Vempati Chinna Satyam, a Padma Bhushan awardee, is well recognized for his efforts for getting classical status to which of the following dance forms?
solution:
The correct answer is **__Kuchipudi__**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Guru Vempati Chinna Satyam**, a **Padma Bhushan awardee** is a Kuchipudi dancer.
 
• He was a renowned Kuchipudi dancer and choreographer who revived the art form and popularized it across India and the world.
 
• He started his own Kuchipudi Dance Academy in Chennai to teach and promote the dance form.
 
• He received many awards and recognitions for his contribution to the art form, including the Padma Bhushan in 1998.
 
• Kelucharan Mohapatra, Uday Shankar, and Guru Bipin Singh were also renowned dancers and choreographers, but they were not associated with the Kuchipudi dance form.
 
• **8 classical dance** forms of India recognized by the **Sangeet Natak Akademi** and the **Ministry of Culture **are as follows.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Kuchipudi

 
 
• Kuchipudi is among one of India's six classical dance forms.
 
• This dance form is a native of the Andhra Pradesh state and is distinct from the other five classical dance forms by incorporating singing.
 
• It first appeared in the 17th century with Sidhyendra Yogi's creation of the dance-drama Bhama Kalapam, which told the tale of Satyabhama, the alluring but envious wife of the Hindu god Krishna.
 
• Holy water is sprinkled and incense is burned before the dance performance starts.
 
• The characters are introduced, the goddesses of knowledge, wealth, and energy are invoked, and songs about each character's role in the play are played.
 
 
 
• The entire male troupe performed the traditional Kuchipudi.
 
• Agnivastra, also known as Bagalbandi, calls for a male dancer to dress in a dhoti (a single pleated piece of cloth hanging down from the waist).
 
• Saris and minimal makeup would be worn by a dancer playing a female role.
 
• The dance-drama performance known as Kuchipudi has its origins in the Natya Shastra, an old Hindu text written in Sanskrit.
 
• In Thanjavur, Kuchipudi is referred to as the Bhagavata Mela and is primarily a Krishna-focused Vaishnavism tradition.
